publication.heroDescription: Essential science and technology news, simplified.

sections.title: People & Politics
sections.description: Important developments in governments, societies and the people shaping the world.

cards.title: Pope Leo XIV Undergoes Surgery for Lung Cancer
cards.content: Pope Leo XIV 71 has been diagnosed with lung cancer and had surgery to remove a lower lobe of his right lung. The surgery was successful and the Pope is expected to stay in hospital for about a week. The Vatican says the cancer was detected during routine checks and was removed to ensure the procedure was radical. The Pope will remain in hospital until October 20 to recover.

cards.title: Russian authorities charge Japanese journalist with espionage
cards.content: Russian authorities have charged a Japanese journalist Yuki Imai with espionage for gathering information about Moscow's defense capabilities for Tokyo. Imai was detained in Russia's far eastern region of Sakhalin a day before he was due to leave the country. Russia claims Imai was acting on the instructions of Japan's national intelligence service to gather information about people involved in a special military operation on the Kuril Islands which Japan claims as its own.

cards.title: Indian Politicians Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka Arrested for Trespassing
cards.content: Two leaders of India's Cockroach Janta Party Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were arrested for trespassing at a protest site in Delhi. They climbed over a locked gate and crossed barricades to enter the site. The activists were protesting for electoral reforms and the resignation of India's top election official over allegations of vote fraud. The police accused them of trespassing and other charges and a magistrate sent them to jail for five days to help with the investigation.

sections.title: Science and technology
sections.description: Discover breakthroughs in science, space, computing and emerging technology.

cards.title: Pentagon sued over ban on AI company's technology
cards.content: Anthropic a US-based AI company is asking a Washington D.C. court to reconsider its appeal after being blacklisted by the Pentagon for refusing to use its AI models for mass surveillance or lethal autonomous warfare. The company's models help with national defense but it declined to allow them to be used for these purposes. The Pentagon had blocked defense contractors from using Anthropic's technology and a previous court decision upheld this ban. Anthropic claims the decision was retaliation for its public discussions about AI safety and a separate court has ruled that the Pentagon's actions violate Anthropic's First Amendment rights.

cards.title: Cramer: Don't Give Up on Semiconductors Despite Oil, Interest Rate Pressure
cards.content: CNBC's Jim Cramer thinks people shouldn't give up on semiconductor stocks just yet. He thinks they're being affected by rising oil prices and interest rates but notes that chip stocks are trading together hiding strong demand for them. Cramer points to Apple's advanced devices which require more computing power as an example of how chips are used in unexpected places. He highlights Micron a memory chip maker as a company with strong fundamentals and a 26-year contract with customers that guarantees revenue.

cards.title: Dell Calls for AI Safeguards to Prevent Harm
cards.content: Dell Technologies CEO Michael Dell believes that artificial intelligence models need safeguards and controls to prevent harm. He thinks that while technology can be powerful it can also be misused and that companies building AI tools need to set limits. Dell agrees that government has a role in regulating AI but didn't specify what that would look like. He also addressed the rise in opposition to data centers saying it's a good thing that people are discussing and working to make them more efficient.

sections.title: Health & wellness
sections.description: Medical research, public health and discoveries that affect everyday wellbeing.

cards.title: New Prosthetic Ear Gives 74-Year-Old Man Hearing on Left Side
cards.content: Stephen Gilbert 74 from Aghalee was born with a rare condition that left him unable to hear on one side. He was recently fitted with a new prosthetic ear that accommodates a hearing aid allowing him to hear on his left side for the first time. Gilbert was born without an ear on one side and had artificial ears made repaired and adapted over the past 29 years. He's grateful for the new prosthetic ear which makes him feel less self-conscious when his ear is exposed and helps him hear in a way he never could before.

cards.title: Pope Leo XIV Undergoes Successful Lung Cancer Surgery
cards.content: Pope Leo XIV had surgery to remove a lung cancer nodule from his right lung. The cancer was a common type called pulmonary adenocarcinoma which grows and spreads slowly. Surgery is often the first step in treating this type of cancer. The pope should have a good prognosis since the cancer was detected early and removed. He will need to follow a recovery plan and avoid respiratory infections. It's unclear what caused the cancer but it's not related to smoking.

cards.title: GLP-1 medication slows aging process, study finds
cards.content: Scientists have found that a type of medication called GLP-1 may slow down the aging process. This medication is typically used to help people with diabetes and weight loss. Studies have shown that it can improve the health of many parts of the body lowering the risk of certain diseases. Researchers have been studying how GLP-1 affects the aging process by looking at biomarkers or biological signs of aging. They found that the medication seemed to slow down aging in people who took it reducing their biological age by 3-6 years. The study's leader says that the effects of the medication are mostly due to weight loss and blood sugar control. Other studies have found similar results showing that GLP-1 medications may have anti-aging effects.

sections.title: Environment
sections.description: Climate, oceans, ecosystems and the changing planet around us.

cards.title: Climate change linked to skin disease rise in nearly half of world's countries.
cards.content: A recent study looked at how climate change affects skin health around the world. It found that over 40% of countries reported changes in skin diseases due to climate change with poorer countries being hit hardest. In fact more than half of countries in low-income and middle-income areas reported these changes. The study also found that certain regions like the Pacific and Mediterranean areas were most affected. The researchers said that climate change is already causing problems with skin diseases especially in poorer countries and that we need to pay more attention to this issue.

cards.title: Flash Flood in Nepal Destroys Homes, Sweeps Away Bridges
cards.content: A flash flood hit Nepal's Himalayan foothills destroying dozens of homes and sweeping away several bridges. The flood which happened on October 11 was caused by a landslide blocking the Budhi Gandaki River creating a temporary barrier that eventually gave way and unleashed a sudden surge downstream. At least five people are missing and the flood damaged three hydropower projects four bridges and affected electricity and telecommunications infrastructure. The Nepali Army rescued 95 people including nine foreign nationals and authorities urged residents to move to safer areas.

cards.title: Global Temperatures Reach 16.27°C in September, 0.82°C Above Average
cards.content: September 2026 was the second hottest September month on record with global temperatures reaching 16.27°C which is 0.82°C above the 1991-2020 average. The record-breaking temperatures were due to a strong El Nino event which is causing extremely high ocean temperatures outside the polar regions. Many regions around the world were drier than normal while others experienced heavy precipitation and floods.

sections.title: Entertainment
sections.description: Stories from film, music, sports, culture and the world of entertainment.

cards.title: Netflix's "La Bola Negra" Emerges as Oscar Contender for Best Picture
cards.content: Christopher Nolan's "The Odyssey" is a top contender for Oscar glory but Netflix's "La Bola Negra" could be the giant-slayer that wins the best picture prize. The Spanish film which premiered at the Cannes Film Festival has been praised for its ambitious and sumptuous portrait of identity repression and queerness. With its unique stories and themes "La Bola Negra" has gained a strong following and could potentially rewrite Netflix's Oscar history. Industry observers think it has the juice to go all the way and give "The Odyssey" a run for its money in most categories.

cards.title: Lena Dunham Revives Girls for Limited Run with Original Cast
cards.content: Lena Dunham the creator of the popular TV show Girls announced that the show will return for a limited run after a 10-year hiatus. The revival will feature five episodes and reunite the original cast including Allison Williams Jemima Kirke Zosia Mamet and Andrew Rannells. Dunham said she's been missing the characters and that they started talking to her again around her 40th birthday. The show will explore what's happened to the characters since they were in their 20s.

cards.title: Rob Brydon Voices New Animated "The Baddies" Adaptation
cards.content: Welsh actor Rob Brydon is voicing a new animated adaptation of the popular children's book "The Baddies" over the Christmas period. The story follows a troll a ghost and a witch as they try to steal a blue spotty hanky from a brave little girl. Brydon will be joined by Gavin and Stacey co-stars Sheridan Smith and Alison Steadman as well as Hammed Animashaun Robyn Cara and Francesca Mills. The half-hour special celebrates kindness and standing up to bullies and features beautiful animation.

sections.title: economy
sections.description: Markets, businesses, trade and economic changes shaping the global economy.

cards.title: Bank of America Fined $1.2 Billion for Failure to Report Suspicious Transactions
cards.content: Bank of America has been fined $1.2 billion for failing to detect and report suspicious transactions including money laundering and illegal activity. The bank didn't report over $5 billion in suspicious transactions some of which posed national security risks. The fine is the third-largest ever imposed by the US Treasury Department and it's a result of the bank relying too much on outside help to detect and report suspicious activity instead of using its own internal controls.

cards.title: IMF predicts UK economy growth, lowest borrowing expected by 2031.
cards.content: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has released its latest forecast for the UK economy which is expected to grow by 1.3% in 2026 up from 1% previously predicted. This is good news as a growing economy means companies will invest more and hire more people and shoppers will have more money to spend. The IMF also says the UK is doing better than other major economies at managing its borrowing and by 2031 it's expected to have the lowest annual borrowing among the G7 countries.

cards.title: Royal Mail faces 400 weekly postal worker exits amid delivery changes
cards.content: About 400 postal workers are leaving Royal Mail every week claims the Communication Workers Union. This number has increased since the company introduced a new delivery system DM26 earlier this year. The union says the new system is causing problems in hundreds of offices with posties prioritizing parcels over letters and wasting time sorting mail. Many postal workers are also saying their workload has increased since the change with some reporting a 25% increase in their daily step count.
